stem: When did the cognitive, emotional, or capacity changes that led you here today first become noticeable?
In the past 30 days, have you had thoughts of hurting yourself or ending your life — even passing ones?
In the past 12 months, have you felt afraid of a partner, family member, or someone in your household — or felt controlled by them in a way that limited your choices?
In the past 30 days, has your alcohol or substance use increased in a way that concerns you — or that someone close to you has raised concerns about?
In the past 30 days, have you had any periods of unusually high energy lasting several days at a time, with reduced need for sleep and rapid thoughts or speech?
In the past 30 days, have you experienced sounds, sights, or sensations that others did not seem to experience — or had thoughts that felt forced or placed into your mind from outside?
In the past 90 days, have you noticed an unusually rapid change in your thinking, memory, or awareness — or had moments of disorientation or confusion?
In the past 30 days, have you been unable to complete basic self-care — eating, hygiene, or essential daily tasks — for several days at a time?
In the past 30 days, how often have you started something important the same day you decided to do it?
In the past 30 days, how often have you been able to start a task you were dreading without an external deadline forcing you?
In the past 30 days, how often have you been able to deliver fully on a high-stakes external deadline — even when other parts of your life were neglected to do it?
In the past 30 days, how often have you known exactly what to do and still been unable to make yourself begin?
In the past 30 days, how often have personal tasks that matter to you — your own appointments, paperwork, or health follow-up — sat untouched while tasks for other people got done?
In the past 30 days, how often have you spent more energy avoiding a task than the task itself would have taken?
In the past 30 days, how often have you struggled to act on important things because the payoff or consequence felt too far away?
In the past 30 days, how often have you been able to work on one thing for 30 minutes without your attention pulling somewhere else?
In the past 30 days, how often have you been able to fully tune out your environment and concentrate when you really needed to?
In the past 30 days, how often have you started reading or listening to something and realized minutes in that you’ve absorbed nothing?
In the past 30 days, how often have you lost the thread of a conversation, meeting, or document and had to ask someone to repeat what was just covered?
In the past 30 days, how often has switching between tasks left you unable to remember what you were doing five minutes earlier?
In the past 30 days, how often have you been able to sustain mental effort across the day without crashing?
In the past 30 days, how often have you experienced cognitive fatigue out of proportion to what you actually did?
In the past 30 days, how often has your recovery time after a demanding day or week been longer than it used to be?
In the past 30 days, how often has your mental energy run out before the day’s required tasks were done?
In the past 30 days, how often have you been able to let a small criticism go within an hour of receiving it?
In the past 30 days, how often have you reacted more strongly than you wanted to when you felt criticized, dismissed, or misunderstood?
In the past 30 days, how often has a small frustration cascaded into a much bigger emotional response?
In the past 30 days, how often have you rehearsed a perceived slight or mistake long after the moment passed?
In the past 30 days, how often have you been able to follow multi-step instructions without writing them down or losing the thread?
In the past 30 days, how often have you walked into a room or opened an app and forgotten what you came for?
In the past 30 days, mid-sentence with someone who mattered — a patient, a client, your child — how often has the word you needed simply not come?
In the past 30 days, how often have you forgotten something important until the moment it was needed?
In the past 30 days, how often have you been able to pause before responding when you felt the urge to react quickly?
In the past 30 days, how often have you interrupted someone, blurted something out, or sent a message you wished you hadn’t?
In the past 30 days, how often have you started something on impulse — a project, purchase, or decision — that you later regretted or couldn’t sustain?
In the past 30 days, how often have you been able to break a complex task into ordered steps and follow them in order?
In the past 30 days, how often have important things slipped through because you didn’t have a system to catch them?
In the past 30 days, how often have you stared at a task knowing it was important but unable to figure out where to start?
In the past 30 days, how often have piles of papers, tabs, emails, or unfinished projects accumulated faster than you could process them?
In the past 30 days, how often have you estimated how long a task would take and finished in the time you planned?
In the past 30 days, how often have you lost track of time and arrived late, rushed, or unprepared to something that mattered?
In the past 30 days, how often have tasks taken two or three times longer than you expected?
In the past 30 days, how often has “just one more thing” before you leave or transition turned into far longer than you had?
